[[File:Jos Engelen.jpg|thumb|Jos Engelen (December 2003).]]
'''Joseph Johannus Engelen''' (born 6 July 1950 in [[Maasniel]]), a [[Dutch people|Dutch]] [[physicist]], was Chairman of the [[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research]] (NWO) from January 2009 to October 2016.<ref name="CERN_Courier">{{cite journal|title=Faces and places: Engelen takes on role as NWO chair in the Netherlands|journal=CERN Courier|date=January 2009|volume=49|issue=1|page=27|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734320}}</ref><ref>[http://www.nwo.nl/en/news-and-events/news/2016/board-transfer-nwo-with-effect-from-1-october-2016.html Board Transfer NWO, Oct. 2016]</ref>

== Career ==
Jos Engelen studied physics at the [[Radboud University Nijmegen]] where he obtained an [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree in 1973. After graduation he worked at the same university as a researcher and lecturer, and gained also his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree here in 1979. From 1979 to 1985 Engelen worked at [[CERN]], the European research centre for particle physics in [[Geneva]], [[Switzerland]].<ref name="CV">{{cite web |last1=Engelen |first1=Jos |title=Curriculum vitae : Jos Engelen |url=https://www.nikhef.nl/~h02/cv_je.pdf |website=Homepage Jos Engelen |publisher=Nikhef |accessdate=11 September 2019}}</ref>

In 1985, he accepted a position at the Dutch National Institute for Subatomic Physics, [[NIKHEF|Nikhef]]. He became professor of Experimental Physics at the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1987. At CERN and DESY (Hamburg, Germany) he carried out experiments in the area of the strong interaction, hard photoproduction and dispersion in deep inelastic collisions.<ref name="CERN_Courier" /><ref name="PubList">{{cite web |title=List of publications : Jos Engelen |url=http://inspirehep.net/author/profile/J.Engelen.1 |website=Inspire HEP |accessdate=11 September 2019}}</ref> He also developed initiatives for research in the field of astroparticle physics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Astroparticle Physics European Coordination |url=https://slideplayer.fr/slide/1327679/ |website=SlidePlayer |accessdate=11 September 2019}}</ref>

From 2001 to 2003 Engelen was director of Nikhef and in 2004 he became the Chief Scientific Officer of [[CERN]], a position he held until 2008.<ref>''International Geneva Yearbook 2005-2006, Organization and Activities of International Institutions in Geneva: v. 19'', United Nations, {{ISBN|978-9210001540}}, p. 301</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Engelen|first1=Jos|title=A word from the CSO: The LHC experiments are going on-line|journal=CERN Bulletin|date=8 September 2008|volume=37-38|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1124113}}</ref> His responsibilities included overseeing the construction and commissioning of the new [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC) particle accelerator and the associated experimental set-ups. From 2007 to 2008 Engelen was chair of ASTRON, the NWO research institute for radio astronomy.<ref>{{cite web |title=UvA Physicist Jos Engelen appointed Chairman NWO |url=https://www.uva.nl/en/content/news/news/2008/08/uva-physicist-jos-engelen-appointed-chairman-nwo.html?1568215589851&1568215698713&1568215721847 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190911152848/https://www.uva.nl/en/content/news/news/2008/08/uva-physicist-jos-engelen-appointed-chairman-nwo.html?1568215589851&1568215698713&1568215721847 |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 September 2019 |website=UvA |publisher=Universiteit van Amsterdam |accessdate=11 September 2019}}</ref>
